title: The magic knot yarn join
subtitle: How to join two yarn ends invisibly within the fabric using an interlocking slip knot
excerpt: The magic knot joins two yarn ends inside the fabric so neither end needs weaving in. The join is strong and almost invisible when done correctly, but it is permanent.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book.

glossaryTerms.definition: A yarn-joining method that uses two interlocking slip knots to join two yarn ends. The knot sits inside the fabric and the tails are trimmed close.
The loose end of yarn left after cutting at a fastened-off point or at a join.

content.text: The
magic knot
joins two yarn ends by looping each tail around the other strand and pulling tight. When both loops are tightened and trimmed, the join disappears into the fabric. No
yarn tails
need weaving in. The join is permanent; it cannot be undone after trimming.
When to use the magic knot
When joining a new ball of the same yarn mid-row where the colours are identical and the join will not be visible.
For dense, non-elastic fabric (amigurumi, baskets) where the knot will not be stressed by stretch.
When not to use the magic knot
Silk, slippery, or superwash-treated yarn: these fibres have low surface friction and the knot can slip through.
Items that will be heavily stretched (socks, elastic garments): the join may not hold under repeated stress.
Lace or open-stitch work: the knot is visible as a slightly thicker point in the strand.
Working the magic knot
Cross the two yarn ends over each other so each strand passes over the other, leaving tails of about 15 cm.
With tail A, form a loop around strand B and pass the tail through the loop. Pull to tighten a slip knot around strand B.
With tail B, form a loop around strand A and pass the tail through the loop. Pull to tighten a slip knot around strand A.
Pull both working strands (not the tails) firmly in opposite directions. The two slip knots slide together and lock against each other.
Test the join by pulling hard on both working strands. If it holds, trim the tails close to the knot.
Common problems

items.symptom: The knot slips apart under tension
items.cause: The slip knots were not tightened enough, or the yarn fibre has low friction.
items.fix: Re-do the join and pull both working strands much harder when locking the knots. On slippery yarn, use a Russian join instead.

items.symptom: There is a visible lump at the join point
items.cause: The knot is sitting on the face of the fabric rather than inside the stitch.
items.fix: When joining, position the knot to sit inside the next stitch worked, not between stitches. The stitch wraps around the knot and hides it.

content.text: What to try next

For slippery yarns or anything that will face significant stretch, use the Russian join instead. The Russian join weaves each tail back through the strand itself, creating a join that holds without relying on friction alone.
